requirements.requirement: Forward node2 messages tagged as the inventory application to node1 and persist them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log.
requirements.summary: The receiver and forwarder configurations validated, rsyslog was active, and multiple inventory-tagged markers sent from node2 appeared at the exact required path on node1. The final observation also showed an established TCP connection and a nonempty persistent file.

requirements.requirement: Keep the centralized log flow and stored data working after node1 restarts.
requirements.summary: Evidence shows a healthy pre-restart listener and stored marker, restart scheduling and bounded unavailability, a changed boot identity, restoration of rsyslog and the listener, retention of prior data, and successful receipt of two new node2 inventory markers after recovery.

requirements.requirement: Keep the centralized log flow working after node2 restarts.
requirements.summary: A healthy forwarding baseline was demonstrated before restart. Evidence then shows restart scheduling and bounded unavailability, a changed boot identity, recovered and enabled rsyslog, retained forwarding configuration, a re-established TCP session, and successful centralized receipt of a new inventory marker.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct transition evidence covers healthy baselines, actual restarts of both nodes, changed boot identities, recovered services and connections, retained data, and successful post-restart end-to-end delivery. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively complete for both managed nodes and agrees with the fixed boot-identity observations.
limitations: End-to-end tests used synthetic messages generated with logger and the inventory tag; no running inventory application workload was observed or exercised directly.
The first marker sent shortly after node1 restarted was not found, although two subsequent markers were received successfully and demonstrated recovered flow.

The generic after-executor listening-socket snapshots were empty despite nearby direct ss observations showing the required listener and connection; the direct task-specific observations are more detailed, but this discrepancy modestly lowers confidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The receiver directory/configuration and rsyslog restart on node1, forwarder configuration and restart on node2, bounded logger probes, and serial node restarts all directly supported task completion, verification, or the mandatory restart protocol. The temporary reboot log did not remain after restart. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services or package damage; changed temporary systemd directories are normal reboot artifacts.
